en_alt: They broadcast the news on the radio.
note: Impersonal 3pl передали also renders as an active English clause; both should pass the word-bank.

en_alt: We were listening to music on the radio.
note: Imperfective слушали is equally the past continuous.

ru: Я был там то́лько оди́н раз.
en_alt: I was there only one time.
note: The literal 'one time' keeps раз visible as the headword.

en_alt: Call me once more.
note: Equally natural rendering of ещё раз.

en_alt: The development of science is moving quickly.
note: 'is going quickly' is acceptable but 'moving' reads more naturally for идёт here.

en_alt: The school helps children's development.
note: Common English phrasing of the same sentence.

ru: Я не хочу́ начина́ть э́тот разгово́р.
en_alt: I don't want to begin this conversation.
note: начинать is 'begin' as readily as 'start'.

en_alt: They gave him permission to work.
note: The active reading matches the 3pl impersonal дали directly.

en_alt: You must not enter without permission.
note: Closer to нельзя, which is a prohibition on the addressee.

en_alt: The friends went through a difficult break-up.
note: тяжёлый is as often 'difficult' as 'hard' in this collocation.
English 'bursts' is correct for разрывы снарядов but the headword gloss 'break' does not cover the explosion sense — the gloss may be the half to widen.

en_alt: The breaking off of relations was unexpected.
note: Alternative natural rendering of разрыв отношений.

en_alt: Reason distinguishes a person.
note: человек is glossed 'person'; the alt keeps the tap-hint aligned.

en_alt: He acted contrary to reason.
note: вопреки is 'contrary to' as well as 'against'.

ru: В саду́ бы́ло как в раю́.
en_alt: In the garden it was like paradise.
note: Russian word order is equally natural in English here.

en_alt: This island is a true paradise.
note: настоящий renders as 'true' as readily as 'real'.

en_alt: The enemy launched several rockets.
note: выпустил is 'launched' as well as 'fired'.

en_alt: Changes have occurred in the timetable.
note: Literal rendering that keeps произошли visible.

en_alt: The lessons run according to the timetable.
note: 'run' is the usual English verb for lessons on a timetable.
'separation' is right for расставание here, but the headword gloss 'break-up' does not cover the neutral parting sense — the gloss may be what needs widening.

ru: На большо́м расстоя́нии ничего́ не ви́дно.

note: 'mortar' is the only correct English for what a bricklayer mixes, but the headword gloss 'solution' does not cover it — the gloss is likely the defective half.

en_alt: It is necessary to cut expenses.
note: надо is impersonal; the English 'we' is supplied, so the impersonal reading should also be accepted.

en_alt: She keeps a record of expenses.
note: вести учёт is 'keep a record' as much as 'keep track'.

en_alt: The child is sleeping in bed.
note: English normally drops the article in 'in bed'.

ru: Ребя́та сыгра́ли в футбо́л во дворе́.
en: The guys played football in the yard.
en_alt: The kids played football in the yard.
note: The other four sentences of this word all render ребята as 'guys', which is also the headword gloss; 'kids' made the tap-hint disagree with the sentence.

en_alt: Guys, help me with the problem.
note: задача is glossed 'problem' and is the usual word for a school maths problem.

ru: Я ви́жу на́ших ребя́т в па́рке.
Он не мог спра́виться с ре́вностью.

en_alt: Jealousy tormented him.
note: The active order matches the Russian clause structure exactly.

en_alt: Many perished during the revolution.
note: погибнуть is glossed 'to perish'; the alt keeps that visible.

en_alt: The revolution began in autumn.
note: Article-free 'in autumn' is equally standard British English.

en_alt: The editorial office put out a new issue.
note: выпустить is 'put out' as well as 'released'.

en_alt: I planted radishes in the vegetable garden.
note: огород is specifically a kitchen/vegetable garden, not a garden in general.

en: There is a lot of water in radishes.
en_alt: Radishes contain a lot of water.
note: English does not use 'radish' as a mass noun, so 'a lot of water in radish' reads wrong; the plural is the natural equivalent of the Russian collective singular.

en: He lives by a tough regime.
en_alt: He lives by a strict regime.
note: жёсткий and стро́гий (the next sentence) were both rendered 'strict', collapsing two different adjectives onto one English word.

en_alt: The doctor prescribed a strict regimen.
note: 'regimen' is the usual English noun in a medical context.

en: Several regimes have succeeded one another in the country.
en_alt: The country has been through several regimes.
note: 'Several regimes have changed' reads in English as the regimes altering themselves, not as смениться — one regime replacing another.

en_alt: The prize was awarded to young directors.
note: вручить is glossed 'awarded'; the alt keeps the tap-hint aligned.

en_alt: The director shot a new film.
note: снять фильм is 'shoot a film' as well as 'make'.

en_alt: We were waiting for the result of the exam.
note: ждали is imperfective; the past continuous is the more everyday rendering.

ru: Учёные подели́лись с журнали́стами пе́рвыми результа́тами.

en_alt: We are happy with the result of the match.
note: Equally natural rendering of доволен.

ru: Он не сли́шком доверя́ет таки́м результа́там.
en_alt: He does not trust such results very much.
note: 'too much' at the end is slightly awkward; 'very much' is the smoother order.

ru: На се́верных ре́ках лёд стои́т до апре́ля.
en_alt: On the northern rivers the ice stays until April.
note: стоит is 'stays' as much as 'holds' for ice.

en_alt: A boat is sailing along the river.
note: плыть covers powered movement too, which 'floats' alone does not suggest.

en_alt: The train went off the rails.
note: Equally standard English for сойти с рельсов.

en: He tightened his belt a bit more.
en_alt: He pulled his belt tighter.
note: поту́же ('a bit tighter') was dropped entirely from the English.

en_alt: Repairs are under way in the flat.
note: The idiomatic 'is being renovated' hides ремонт; the literal alt teaches the headword.

en_alt: They finished the repairs in a month.
note: English normally pluralises 'repairs' for building work.

en_alt: The car needs repairs.
note: Both the mass and plural forms are idiomatic here.

en_alt: She puts mascara on her eyelashes.
note: 'paints' is literal but the mascara collocation is the everyday English.

ru: В дороги́х рестора́нах ча́сто игра́ет жива́я му́зыка.
en_alt: Live music often plays in expensive restaurants.
note: The English-order version is smoother; both should be accepted.

en_alt: We are having dinner in the restaurant.
note: 'in' and 'at' are both natural for в ресторане.
'prescription' is the only correct English here, but the headword gloss 'recipe' does not cover that sense of рецепт — the gloss likely needs widening.

en: We crossed the small river over the little bridge.
en_alt: We crossed the small river by the little bridge.
note: 'crossed the river by the bridge' reads as 'beside the bridge' in English; по мостику is movement across it.

en_alt: They discussed all the possible solutions.
note: 'all the possible decisions' is stilted; решения in this frame is normally 'solutions'.

en_alt: The bird was sitting behind the grating.
note: сидела is imperfective, so the past continuous is equally right.

en_alt: Please boil the rice.
note: сварить is specifically to boil; both renderings are natural.

ru: На у́жин был рис с овоща́ми.

en_alt: They make beautiful items from horn.
note: The impersonal 3pl делают also renders actively.
'gender' is correct for род in a grammatical context but the headword gloss 'family' does not cover it, so the tap-hint contradicts the sentence.

ru: В на́шем роду́ все до́лго живу́т.
en_alt: In our family everyone lives a long time.
note: 'lives long' is terse; 'a long time' is the ordinary English.

ru: В чужо́м го́роде она́ ча́сто вспомина́ет о роди́телях.
en_alt: In a strange city she often remembers her parents.
note: вспоминать is glossed 'to remember'; the alt keeps the tap-hint aligned.

ru: Взро́слый сын до сих пор помога́ет роди́телям.
Ста́ршая дочь ка́ждую неде́лю пи́шет свои́м роди́телям.
В о́тпуск я е́зжу к мо́рю вме́сте с роди́телями.
en_alt: On holiday I go to the sea together with my parents.
note: о́тпуск is specifically annual leave, so 'on holiday' is the closer British rendering.

en_alt: The decision rested with the parents.
note: остаться за кем-то is 'rest with someone', which the alt makes explicit.

en_alt: A cold spring was gushing out from under the stone.
note: бил is imperfective past, so the continuous is equally right.
